env.world: The observed-data experiment for a lower-threshold modified treatment policy. The baseline-stratum space is finite, \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,J\}\); the treatment is continuous, \(A\in[0,1]\); the outcome is bounded, \(Y\in[0,1]\); and the observed unit is \(O=(X,A,Y)\), with \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) drawn independently from one law \(P\). Each \(P\) carries the stratum masses \(p_x=P(X=x)\), a Borel conditional treatment density \(\pi_x\) with \(P(A\in B\mid X=x)=\int_B\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\), and a continuous outcome regression \(\mu_x^P\) that is a version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\). The lower-threshold clamp \(d_\delta(a)=\max\{a,\delta\}\) produces the conditional atom mass \(q_x(\delta)=\int_0^\delta\pi_x(a)\,\mathrm da\), the retained natural-course mean \(\nu_\delta(P)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mathbf 1\{A>\delta\}]\), and the observed-data target \(\theta_\delta(P)=\nu_\delta(P)+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}p_xq_x(\delta)\mu_x^P(\delta)\). The finite-stratum clamp model \(\mathcal M\) is the class of laws satisfying the conditional-density, stratum-mass, polynomial-thinning, and Hölder member conditions.

env.world: The realized-design local-polynomial experiment inside one baseline stratum. The sample is split into three deterministic blocks \(I_0,I_1,I_2\) with \(|I_j|\geq\lfloor n/4\rfloor\). Writing \(U_i=(A_i-\delta_n)/h_n\) and \(v_\ell(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^\ell)^\top\), the design carries the normalized reference moment matrices \(M_{\kappa,\rho}=\{\int_0^1v_\ell(u)v_\ell(u)^\top(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}/\{\int_0^1(\rho+u)^\kappa\,\mathrm du\}\) with uniform constant \(\lambda_\star=(c_-/c_+)\inf_{\rho\geq0}\lambda_{\min}(M_{\kappa,\rho})\), the local count \(N_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,\delta_n\leq A_i\leq\delta_n+h_n\}\), the unnormalized Gram \(G_x=\sum_{i\in I_2}\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}v_\ell(U_i)v_\ell(U_i)^\top\), the good-design event \(\Omega_x=\{N_x>0,\ \lambda_{\min}(G_x)\geq\lambda_\star N_x/2\}\), and the exact intercept weights \(w_{ix}=\mathbf 1\{X_i=x,0\leq U_i\leq1\}e_0^\top G_x^{-1}v_\ell(U_i)\) on \(\Omega_x\), \(w_{ix}=0\) off it. From these are built the sample-split total-Gram-stabilized estimator \(\widehat\theta_n\) and the bias-aware interval \(\mathrm{CI}_n\) with its local atom fallback on singular-Gram events. The same realized design supports a candidate sharp radius. For a realized design \(z\) and an admissible affine weight vector \(w\) supported on the local window and reproducing every monomial through degree \(\ell\) at the threshold, \(\operatorname{exactHolderBias}_{z,x}(w)\) is the supremum of \(|\sum_{i\in I_2}w_if(A_i)-f(\delta_n)|\) over the \([0,1]\)-valued Hölder class \(\mathcal H_{\beta,L}\); \(\operatorname{realizedExactModulus}_{z,x}(t)\) is the infimum over such \(w\) of that bias plus \(t(\sum_{i\in I_2}w_i^2)^{1/2}\), totalized to zero when no admissible weight exists; \(\operatorname{exactModulusHandle}\) is its integral under the \(n\)-fold independent observed-design law; and \(\operatorname{worstExactModulus}_n(t)\) is the supremum of that integral over \(P\in\mathcal M\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\). These are radius, or half-length, quantities; the zero value on an empty feasible set only totalizes the candidate, and no honesty, nondegeneracy or optimality of an interval using it is asserted here. The split itself may also be chosen as a sequence: an admissible deterministic three-way split \(B_n=(I_0,I_1,I_2)\) at sample size \(n\) determines every object above, and \(B_\bullet=(B_n)_{n\geq1}\) denotes a sequence of such splits, which may depend on the deterministic threshold sequence but not on the realized data.

env.world: The structural full-data overlay carrying the causal target. On a standard Borel latent state space \(\mathcal U\) there is a latent response variable \(U\) and, for each \(x\in\mathcal X\), a jointly Borel measurable structural response map \(g_x:[0,1]\times\mathcal U\to[0,1]\); the potential-outcome process \(a\mapsto Y(a)\) is represented simultaneously outside one null set by \(Y(a)=g_X(a,U)\). A full-data law \(P^{\mathrm F}\) governs \((X,A,Y,U,\{Y(a):a\in[0,1]\})\) and has observed \((X,A,Y)\)-margin \(P\); it carries the full-data response mean \(m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[g_x(a,U)\mid X=x]\) and the clamp-policy mean \(\psi_\delta(P^{\mathrm F})=\mathbb E_{P^{\mathrm F}}[Y\{d_\delta(A)\}]\). Each member carries its OWN standard Borel carrier; no common carrier and no carrier-richness condition is imposed. The structural class \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) collects the full-data laws whose margin lies in \(\mathcal M\) and which satisfy simultaneous latent-response factorization, latent randomization \(A\perp\!\!\!\perp U\mid X\), and fiberwise structural-mean continuity of \(a\mapsto m_x^{\mathrm F}(a)\) on \([0,\bar\delta]\). Over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\), \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) and \(L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\) are the minimax absolute-error risk and the minimax honest expected length among estimators and intervals measurable with respect to the observed sample alone.

citations.title: Foundations of Modern Probability, second edition
citations.citation: Kallenberg, O. (2002). Foundations of Modern Probability, second edition. Springer. Theorem 6.3. doi:10.1007/978-1-4757-4015-8.
citations.verbatim_statement: Let X be a standard Borel space, Y a measurable space, and X and Y corresponding random variables. Then there exists a kernel μ from Y to X satisfying P(X ∈ B | Y) = μ(Y,B) for Borel B, and this kernel is unique almost surely with respect to the law of Y.
